name: PT TBS Energi Utama Tbk

frontmatter.title: TBS Energi Utama — re-marked on the quarterly waste run-rate and a warranted discount
frontmatter.summary: The nine-month release implies a weaker third-quarter waste run-rate than the nine-month average, so the waste mark is re-struck on the quarter and falls. The SOTP now carries the receivable haircut, an independent discount inside the card band and no price anchoring. Coal stays at zero on its allocated debt; HPS is preference equity, not debt. REDUCE, Rp312, -21.2%.
thesis: The nine-month 2026 release confirms the mix - waste plus electric vehicles are 66.0% of revenue and 71.0% of adjusted EBITDA - but the same shares imply Q3 waste-plus-EV EBITDA of only US$31.6m annualised, against the US$42.0m nine-month average annualisation [S25, S12, F145, F203]. The waste mark falls to US$106.2m and the target to Rp312, a -21.2% return - a REDUCE.

The corrected SOTP is independent of the price: after the non-controlling interest and the 40.0% warranted discount, the marked parts are worth Rp258, against today's Rp396; the discount is the top of the card band, not the higher level the old reverse solve produced.

Coal is marked at zero despite US$20.1m of nine-month coal EBITDA: the reserve is a short run-off, mine amortisation and sustaining capex absorb the cash, and the US$120.4m debt proxy costs more than the free cash flow [S25, F189].

Waste is the value: US$31.6m of annualised Q3 waste-plus-EV adjusted EBITDA at the stock's own-history median, less the US$234.8m debt proxy, gives US$106.2m of equity [S25, F145]. The nine-month average mark of US$218.7m is disclosed as the upper bound [F203, F204].

The P/BV cross-check at Rp263 is the honest counterweight, and HPS is preference equity at SBTH: at an assumed high-single to low-double-digit coupon its annual claim is US$32.6m-US$49.0m, ranking ahead of the ordinary shares but adding no parent value on day one [S26].

catalysts.event: EGMS to approve the HPS preference investment in SBTH
NTBE floating-solar project targeted for commercial operation

blocks.text: This revision moves TBS Energi Utama to **REDUCE** with a twelve-month target of **Rp312**, a -21.2% return from the Rp396 price. The trigger is the company's own nine-month release. Waste plus electric vehicles were 91.8% of first-half adjusted EBITDA but only 71.0% of the nine-month figure; applied to the disclosed totals, the difference leaves Q3 waste-plus-EV EBITDA of US$31.6m annualised, far below the US$42.0m nine-month-average annualisation [S25, S12, F145, F203]. The revenue forecast already uses the third-quarter run-rate for the fourth quarter, so the waste mark must use the same period. The rest of the release confirms the transition: revenue US$257.3m, gross profit US$45.2m, adjusted EBITDA US$44.4m, a parent net loss of US$35.4m, operating cash flow US$20.3m and cash US$89.6m [S25].

The rating hinges on that choice, and we state it plainly. On the nine-month-average waste mark the blended target would be about Rp430, which is no longer a REDUCE; on the Q3 run-rate it is Rp312. We use the Q3 run-rate because it is the latest disclosed period, because the revenue build uses it, and because the nine-month average gives the stronger first half a full-year weight. The old HOLD depended on the nine-month average; the corrected mark does not support it. TBS remains a trust-controlled energy holding mid-transition from coal to waste, and the question is what the ordinary shareholder owns after the HPS financing [S9, S25, S26].

The EV/EBITDA leg stays dropped. It was struck at DSSA's multiple - a konglo name whose listed premium the konglo card excludes from a parent's fundamental value - on group LTM EBITDA that includes the coal segment the SOTP marks at zero. The engine reads group EBITDA, and no waste-specific non-konglo comparator is registered, so the leg cannot be rebuilt premium-free on a segment-consistent base. The engine renormalises to 67% SOTP and 33% P/BV; the target is Rp312, a REDUCE [S0, S11, S12, S25].

The breakeven marks are re-solved on the corrected base after the non-controlling interest: parity needs a post-NCI waste mark of US$186.1m, the HOLD floor US$148.4m and the SELL boundary US$91.9m. The nine-month print supports the operating story - an 18.0% gross margin, adjusted EBITDA at 17.0% and operating cash flow of US$20.3m, with coal still contributing US$20.1m of EBITDA - but the Q3 waste slowdown is the new fact the prior update missed [S25, F189].

The discount is no longer reverse-solved from the price. The company does not publish a historical SOTP and the data pack has no NAV series, so a true five-year discount-to-NAV range cannot be sourced; the closest own-history series is P/BV, whose own mean and median are disclosed in the valuation section and whose current trailing level is at that mean [S0]. We use the top of the card's band for the governance reasons below, and the midpoint gives Rp346, still a REDUCE. The P/BV leg and the preference coupon are the counterweights, and the driver bear corner at Rp200 is the path to a SELL [S0, data/base_rates.yaml, F157].

TBS Energi Utama is an Indonesian energy group that began as a thermal-coal miner, listed in 2012 and renamed from Toba Bara Sejahtra in 2022 to mark a shift toward sustainable infrastructure. It reports in US dollars and runs five segments: coal mining, coal trading, waste management, a residual power book after the coal plants were sold, and an "others" line with palm oil, renewables and electric vehicles [S8, S9].

The mix has inverted. In the first half of 2026 waste produced 61.2% of revenue and 91.8% of adjusted EBITDA; by the nine months waste and electric vehicles together were 66.0% of revenue and 71.0% of adjusted EBITDA, and waste alone earned US$157.3m of revenue at a 13.3% gross margin [S12, S25]. Coal is smaller but not negligible in the P&L: mining revenue US$61.8m, gross profit US$21.6m and EBITDA US$20.1m, while trading is down to US$19.5m with a small EBITDA loss [S25]. Waste carries most of the acquired goodwill because it was built by acquisition [S12].

The waste platform, under SBTH Asia Holdings, operates three brands: Cora Environment, a Singapore municipal and commercial collector formerly Sembcorp Environment, with an energy-from-waste plant of about 360,000 tonnes a year; Asia Medical Enviro Services, with about 45.0% of the Singapore medical-waste market; and Arah Environmental in Indonesian medical, industrial and household waste across 15.0 provinces [S9, S10]. Together they collected 755,990 tonnes in the first nine months of 2026, and the economics rest on collection density, permitted facilities and long municipal contracts [S25, S22, S10].

Coal is smaller than the balance sheet suggests: about 7,087 hectares across three East Kalimantan mines run through ABN, IM and TMU, with reserves of about 14 Mt against planned production of 3-4 Mt a year [S9]. In the first half the mines produced 0.8 Mt and sold 0.6 Mt at an average price of US$55.2/ton against a FOB cash cost of US$38.2/ton and a stripping ratio of 3.2x [S12].

The other legs are real but sub-scale: a 6 MW mini-hydro plant, a 46 MWp floating-solar project that was 65.0 complete at the half-year, 13,883 Electrum electric two-wheelers and a 2,185 hectare plantation [S12, S9]. Highland holds 60.4% and PT Toba Sejahtra 8.0% through a Singapore trust, leaving a 31.7% residual; the controlling block sets strategy and how much cash reaches the parent [S9].

TBS straddles two industries with little in common. Thermal coal is a mature, price-taking export business; waste management is a recurring, contract-based service with local density advantages; waste is now the dominant earnings driver even though coal still supplies much of the collateral [S9, S12].

The coal arm is cyclical and small. TBS's realised price of US$55.2/ton sits below the headline HBA and ICI benchmarks because its grades are lower and its mix includes trading volumes, and the FOB cash cost of US$38.2/ton leaves a thin margin; the segment ran an operating loss in the first half [S12, S11]. With about 14.0 Mt of reserves against planned production of 3-4 Mt a year, the coal arm should be valued as a declining cash harvest, not on a stable multiple [S9].

Coal regulation matters three ways: the progressive royalty sets a floor under unit costs, the domestic market obligation requires a share of output at capped prices, and environmental licensing governs expansion and closure. Policy is pushing Indonesia away from coal generation while still relying on it for baseload, a long noisy transition rather than a clean exit [S9].

Waste is the opposite: a recurring service with high local density economics, long municipal contracts and permitted facilities hard to replicate. Singapore's collection is split into geographic sectors, Cora holds two, and its energy-from-waste plant turns non-recyclable waste into industrial steam; AMES's compliance moat gives it about 45.0% of the medical-waste market, while Arah serves a fragmenting Indonesian market [S10, S12, S9]. Competition is local and consolidating, with permits, density and disposal capacity as barriers rather than capital alone; the risk is that the acquisition-led roll-up pays rising multiples faster than it earns synergies, which is where the HPS capital will go [S10, S15]. Renewables are contracted but small, and the EV business lacks a proven durable margin [S12, S9].

External influences are macro and regulatory: dollar reporting, Singapore-dollar waste revenue and rupiah debt mean USD/SGD, USD/IDR and Indonesian rates all matter. The look-through factors - coal, Indonesian rates, Singapore waste demand, USD/SGD and domestic EV and plantation demand - are recorded for sizing [S9, S10, S12].

Revenue fell from US$635.8m in FY2022 to US$365.9m in FY2025 as coal normalised and power moved toward divestment, and gross profit fell faster, from US$136.0m to US$29.7m [S0, S8]. FY2025 also carries a divestment loss of about US$96.9m and a net loss of US$161.9m [S17, S8].

The first half of 2026 shows the post-divestment business: revenue US$173.0m, gross profit more than doubled to US$28.2m, adjusted EBITDA US$25.7m and operating cash flow positive at US$14.6m [S12, S11]. The company's nine-month release extends it: revenue US$257.3m, gross profit US$45.2m at 18.0%, adjusted EBITDA up 39.0% to US$44.4m at a 17.0% margin, the parent loss narrowing 72.0% to US$35.4m, operating cash flow US$20.3m and cash US$89.6m [S25]. It is still an EBITDA improvement, not an earnings improvement: D&A, the Cora acquisition and the refinancing one-off exceed operating profit [S25]. Equity was US$172.0m against US$751.7m of assets and US$579.6m of liabilities at 30 September 2026; gross debt is not disclosed in the release, and the last balance-sheet figure is US$399.3m at 30 June [S20, S25, S11].

Waste produced US$155.4m of FY2025 revenue and most of the first half, while coal mining and trading contributed about a third at a low margin [S3, S12]. We set FY2026E growth at -6.6% - the nine months of US$257.3m plus a fourth quarter at the third-quarter run-rate gives US$341.6m - then 6.0% and 5.0% as waste annualises; no large acquisition is assumed [S25, S12, S26].

We anchor FY2026E gross margin at the exact nine-month 17.6% and operating expenses at the first-half run-rate of 19.2% of revenue, because the data pack's SG&A is too low (FY2025 selling and G&A about US$72.0m, first half US$33.2m) [S8, S12, S25]. The blended margin is mix, not waste economics: waste earns 13.3% while coal mining's gross profit is US$21.6m on US$61.8m of revenue [S25]. The group is EBITDA-positive but EBIT-negative at the run-rate, the arithmetic of a capital-intensive transition. FY2026E carries a one-off refinancing charge; the release gives neither the amount nor the cash/non-cash split, so we carry an explicit range and use the mid-point rather than a figure sized solely to reconcile the parent loss of US$35.4m [S25]. The charge is inside forecast net debt as a cash cost; if it proves non-cash or is amortised, net debt is lower and the SOTP is unaffected because the marks do not use the forecast loss. The one-off is a plug with a disclosed range, not a sourced figure.

The data pack's D&A was the G&A charge only. The audited notes show fixed-asset depreciation US$22.2m, mine-property amortisation US$31.3m, right-of-use depreciation US$11.8m and intangibles US$8.8m, a full charge of US$74.1m [S8]. The nine-month release does not disclose the charge but says Cora-related depreciation and amortisation are largely non-cash; the forecast keeps the post-divestment first-half run-rate of 17.6% of revenue, not the FY2025 ratio that includes divested-PLTU depreciation [S8, S12, S25].

FY2025 operating cash flow was US$5.2m with capex of US$47.1m; the first half improved to US$14.6m against fixed-asset capex of US$10.2m, and nine-month operating cash flow was US$20.3m [S8, S11, S25]. The release does not split nine-month capex, so we keep capex at 10.0% of revenue falling to 8.0% and net borrowing of US$15.0m and US$10.0m [S13, S25]. Net debt was US$307.3m at FY2025 and about 5.4x adjusted EBITDA at the half; cash rose to US$89.6m at 30 September but gross debt is undisclosed, and the refinancing extends maturity, not leverage [S8, S12, S13, S25]. On the disclosed cash and the rise in total liabilities, the 30 September net debt proxy is US$313.8m, essentially flat in dollars; because equity fell, leverage is higher. The valuation section shows a symmetric debt-proxy sensitivity, and the SOTP marks use the 30 June proxies until a gross-debt figure is disclosed [F208].

Cash conversion deteriorated: operating cash flow over restated EBITDA was 1.41 in FY2024, 0.12 in FY2025 and 0.46 in the first nine months, and the negative accruals ratio is mechanical from the non-cash divestment loss [S8, S24]. Goodwill is US$85.5m, about half of parent equity, and the price is 2.22 times tangible book [S11]. The former Highland receivable of US$37.7m was assigned to CDG Trading at 6.8% and sits in US$43.2m of third-party receivables with CDG's ownership undisclosed; we classify it optics-class and apply the half-haircut (Rp263), showing the full write-off (Rp224) against reported book (Rp302); the same half-haircut now sits in the SOTP "others" mark, so the two legs are consistent [S8, S11].

The holdco card calls for a sum of the parts with honest marks, less holdco net debt, less a discount treated as the base rate, not the opportunity; TBS fits it better than a consolidated multiple, which would price the mix and the leverage together [S0].

Cost of equity builds from a risk-free rate of 4.9%, an equity risk premium of 4.2% plus a country premium of 2.5%, and a beta of 0.9 levered to 2.3, giving a cost of equity of 20.3% and a WACC of 10.4% [S0].

Each part is an equity value: coal after its own debt proxy, waste on an EV/EBITDA multiple after its debt proxy, trading and power at book, and others at book less the same half-haircut the P/BV leg carries [S11, S12]. The only deduction is the non-controlling interest of US$21.8m, against an ABN claim of US$29.1m; the full net figure is conservative because coal is marked at zero [S11 p.137]. The US$307.1m book elimination is the consolidation wedge, not third-party debt, and deducting it again was the prior FATAL [S11 p.150].

Coal is zero despite US$20.1m of nine-month coal EBITDA. The rebuilt run-off uses the actual segment volume, price and cash cost: the 14 Mt reserve at the current sales run-rate gives a life of about nine years, while the 3-4 Mt/yr plan gives a shorter four-year life. On the observed volume the free cash flow after sustaining capex and cash tax is a few million dollars a year, and the US$120.4m debt proxy costs more than that, so the equity floors at zero [F207]. Without the debt proxy the same DCF is positive, but the proxy would then have to be deducted at holdco, leaving the SOTP unchanged; the plan-volume upper bound is about the same size as the proxy. The red team is right that the proxy is an allocation, not a secured claim; it is still the only honest way to allocate the group's US$399.3m debt across the parts [S25, S9, S11, F85, F207].

Waste uses the Q3 run-rate, not the nine-month average. Waste plus electric vehicles were 71.0% of the US$44.4m nine-month adjusted EBITDA but 91.8% of the US$25.7m first-half figure; the difference is US$31.6m annualised for Q3 [S25, S12, F145]. At US$106.2m of equity after the US$234.8m debt proxy, the mark is US$341.0m of enterprise value at the own-history median; the nine-month-average alternative is US$218.7m [F203, F204]. The Cora purchase of US$305.9m is the market test; the equity mark is below it because of that debt [S8]. The multiple is the stock's own-history median, not a waste-infrastructure comparator, but no premium-free waste comparator is registered; the scenarios section shows the band.

The debt proxies are 30 June figures. At 30 September the release gives cash of US$89.6m and a higher liability total but no gross debt; the net debt proxy is US$313.8m, close to the 30 June level, so dollar leverage is flat while equity is lower [S20, F208]. A symmetric move in the waste and coal debt proxies takes the target to Rp293 on the high side and Rp331 on the low side, both REDUCE; the base keeps the 30 June proxies because no newer gross-debt figure is disclosed [F214, F215].

The card also requires holdco opex capitalised at about ten times. We have tested it and do not deduct it again. The Q2 segment note reconciles the consolidated selling and G&A charge of US$33.2m to the five segments with no unallocated corporate column, and the waste mark is struck on adjusted EBITDA after segment G&A while the coal run-off uses segment costs after selling and G&A [S11 p.145, S12]. Capitalising the same group cost a second time would double count it. The residual is the "others" book mark, which is carried at net assets less the receivable haircut; if some corporate cost is embedded there it is not separately capitalised, and that is a disclosed limitation rather than a hidden deduction.

The "others" mark now carries the same half-haircut as the P/BV leg: book net assets of US$94.3m less liabilities of US$50.7m less the half of the US$43.2m related-party receivable, giving a materially lower book mark than the full net-asset figure. The full write-off is a downside case at about Rp224 on the P/BV leg and a lower SOTP; the receivable is an optics-class flag, not a manipulation-class one, so a half-haircut is the base [S8, F89, F167].

The blend is 67% SOTP and 33% P/BV. P/BV at the 0.83 peer median gives Rp263, 2.0% below the SOTP; the gap is book quality - already net of the half-haircut (US$145.6m against reported US$167.2m), with US$85.5m of goodwill and the divestment loss [S0, S8, S11]. The median is the engine's trailing P/B of the registered CONGLOMERATES packs at their 30 June 2026 balance sheets and current datapack prices; the red team's later snapshot gives a slightly higher median; the per-share difference is small and does not change the rating. The EV/EBITDA leg is removed; P/E is unavailable on negative trailing earnings and no dividend is forecast, so the honest set is the primary plus one cross-check [S0].

The P/BV leg is also stressed on the forecast book, because the model is EBIT-negative at the current margin structure and the book erodes. On FY2027E book the leg is Rp225 and on FY2028E book lower again; a full impairment of the US$85.5m goodwill takes it to Rp108 [F209, F210]. The operating-leverage path is real - the non-cash coal mine amortisation and the coal segment's G&A roll off as the reserves deplete - but the model holds the ratios flat, so the forecast understates that improvement. We treat the forecast-book stress as a downside cross-check and keep the base leg on current reported book; the primary SOTP does not depend on the P/BV leg [S8, S11, F13, F209, F210].

The base discount is 40.0%, the top of the card's band, not the price's own implied discount. The old figure was reverse-solved from the 30 October price, so the SOTP leg equalled the price by construction and carried no independent information [S0, S25]. The company does not publish a historical SOTP and the data pack has no NAV series, so the five-year discount-to-NAV range the card asks for cannot be sourced; the closest own-history series is P/BV (FY2022 to FY2025, mean and median in the note below), and the current trailing P/B is at that mean, not at a premium [S0]. The top of the band is warranted by governance and upstream coverage: the controlling trust, the undisclosed related-party receivable, the HPS preference ranking ahead of the ordinary and the thin dividend-upstream coverage proxy [S9, S8, S26, F163]. At the band midpoint the target is Rp346, still a REDUCE; the base is Rp312 [data/base_rates.yaml].

Holding coal at zero and the discount fixed, price parity needs a post-NCI waste mark of US$186.1m; the HOLD floor is US$148.4m and the SELL boundary US$91.9m [F113, F119, F120]. At the low end of the waste band the target is Rp200, a SELL; at the twelve-turn level Rp352, at the peer multiple Rp429 and at the Cora anchor Rp275 [F116, F117, F164, F165].

The discount-only bear is Rp278 and the bull Rp346 [S12, S15]. The driver corners are wider - Rp200 for a SELL when waste is at the low end, coal zero and the discount widens, and Rp514 for a BUY at the peer multiple with coal at its plan upper bound - and the probability-weighted driver target is Rp335 [F157-F159]. That weighted figure sits above the scenario-weighted base but still below the current share price at the warranted discount, so it is not in an ADD band; the coal zero floor only limits how far the bear corner can fall.

HPS commits up to S$555m to SBTH in multiple tranches through newly issued preference shares and other instruments, subject to EGMS approval, with TBS retaining control [S26]. It is equity, not debt: it does not enter holdco net debt and there is no bridge line, because a fair-value preference subscription adds cash and an equal prior claim. It sits inside SBTH, below the waste equity mark, which is the ordinary/common equity after that claim; it creates parent value only through what the cash earns [S26, S10]. The coupon is undisclosed; at an assumed high-single to low-double-digit rate the annual claim is US$32.6m-US$49.0m against US$44.4m of nine-month adjusted EBITDA, so it is mezzanine-like in ranking while still preferred equity [S26, F101, F102]. The conversion sensitivity is explicit: a range of common-equivalent stakes would take the target to Rp301, Rp290 and Rp279, all REDUCE [F211-F213]. That is why the bear case treats the ordinary equity as worth little until the coupon is covered, while the base adds no headline value at inception.

**Regulatory risk** is medium-likelihood and high-impact: the royalty schedule, domestic market obligation and environmental licensing can change the coal arm's unit economics, and the waste franchise depends on municipal contracts and permits in two jurisdictions [S9, S10]. **Commodity risk** is high-likelihood and medium-impact: TBS is a price-taker, so a weaker ICI complex would compress the coal cash harvest before waste offsets it [S12, S9]. **Execution risk** is medium-likelihood and high-impact: the waste platform is acquisition-led, the HPS money is staged, and the solar project must reach commercial operation on schedule [S12, S10].

**Governance risk** is medium-likelihood and high-impact: Highland holds 60.4% and PT Toba Sejahtra 8.0% through a Singapore trust, and a preference claim ranks ahead of the ordinary at the waste subsidiary; the inbreng was completed without a fairness opinion because the entities are almost wholly owned [S9, S10, S16]. **Liquidity risk** is medium-likelihood and medium-impact: the residual outside the controlling holders is 31.7%, and the average daily traded value of IDR13.3bn is thin against a market capitalisation of IDR3,290.6bn [S0]. **Currency and rate risk** is medium-likelihood and medium-impact: dollar reporting, Singapore-dollar waste revenue and rupiah debt mean a stronger dollar or higher Indonesian rates compress translated value [S8, S13]. **Coal reserve risk** is the quiet one: a short reserve life turns the cash harvest into a run-off if reserves are not replaced [S9].

The bear case is now explicit rather than implied by the discount. The Q3 waste run-rate is the base; if it persists rather than recovers, the ordinary equity earns nothing until waste EBITDA covers the preference coupon and segment interest, and the "others" book mark carries the related-party receivable at half value with the US$85.5m goodwill unimpaired. Leverage is 5.4x net loans to adjusted EBITDA at the half, cash conversion is 0.46 operating cash flow to EBITDA at the nine months, and a coupon at the low end of the assumed range would absorb more than half of the nine-month annualised adjusted EBITDA [S12, S25, F101, F102, F156]. A common-equivalent HPS conversion at the low end of the range alone takes the target to Rp301 [F211]. On a full goodwill impairment the P/BV leg is Rp108 [F210]. None of these is the base, but together they are the path to the SELL corner at Rp200.

The dated bull case the red team asked for is HPS deployed at the Cora-like multiple, the solar project reaching commercial operation on its stated schedule and waste revenue compounding. The HPS commitment is a dated EGMS event and the funds are earmarked for Asian waste expansion; the floating-solar project was 65.0 complete with commercial operation targeted for the fourth quarter [S26, S12]. If the HPS capital is deployed at the Cora acquisition multiple and waste revenue grows at its nine-month rate, the waste mark moves toward the peer-multiple case and the target toward Rp429; with the discount also narrowing to the band midpoint the target is the bull scenario value below [S25]. We do not treat the EGMS itself as a discount-narrowing catalyst: it authorises a preference issuance that ranks ahead of the ordinary, so it changes the capital structure before it changes the discount [S26, F195].

The scenarios mirror the same driver, the holdco discount, at probabilities of 25.0%, 50.0% and 25.0%; the values are Rp278, Rp312 and Rp346 [S12, S15]. The engine can shock only model inputs, so the operating distribution is given as computed facts: the waste band runs from Rp200 to Rp429, and the discount-shocked corners are Rp200 and Rp514 [F116, F164, F157, F158]. A SELL requires the waste multiple to compress to the low end while the discount widens, the mirrored operating downside, not the central path [S12, S0].

The signposts that would change our view are specific: a segment disclosure letting us mark waste on its own cash flows; a completed, priced acquisition showing the HPS money deployed accretively; a reserve upgrade or long-term offtake extending mine life; and a dated discount-narrowing event such as a buyback, tender or structural dividend increase from the waste subsidiary [S10, S15]. On the other side, a preference term sheet giving HPS conversion or upside participation at the expense of the ordinary would widen the discount, not narrow it [S10, S15].

Control is concentrated and the structure opaque at the top. Highland Strategic Holdings holds 60.4% and PT Toba Sejahtra 8.0%; Highland is owned by GLAS Trust, a Singapore trust acting for a passive private investment trust, and no single individual holds more than half [S9]. The annual report leaves 31.7% outside those holders; the data pack's free-float and insider fields overlap and sum above one hundred per cent, so we use the filing composition [S9]. Minorities have little influence over strategy, related-party terms or the pace of the transition [S9].

The auditor is KAP Purwantono, Sungkoro & Surja, an EY member, which issued an unqualified opinion on the FY2025 statements signed by the board on 9 March 2026 [S9]. Related-party dealings are small in the reported numbers but structurally important. At FY2024 the group carried a non-current receivable from Highland of US$37.7m under an acknowledgement extended to eighteen years and then assigned on 30 June 2025 to CDG Trading at 6.8%; the balance now sits in US$43.2m of non-current third-party receivables, and CDG's ownership and relationship to the controller are not disclosed [S8]. Interest income from Highland was US$0.7m in FY2025, so the receivable is not dead, but the assignment to an undisclosed third party is exactly the channel through which value can move between affiliates; we classify it optics-class and apply the haircut in the P/BV leg [S8].

On 16 October 2026 the group moved its SBT shares through SBTI, SBTH and SBTG at a stated S$138.2m with no fairness opinion because the entities are almost wholly owned [S16]. It is an intra-group subscription price, not an appraisal, so we treat it as a weak marker; the sequencing matters because the waste opco sits under SBTH immediately before HPS takes preference shares there, directing the claim at the whole platform [S10, S16].

On pledges, the company's shares in operating subsidiaries and its accounts, receivables and inventories are collateral for the ADB, TLB and SEF facilities, while the controlling shareholder's TOBA shares are not disclosed as pledged; a subsidiary pledge is normal project finance, a controlling-block pledge would be a margin-call supply risk [S9]. The group paid US$17.5m of dividends in FY2025 including minorities despite a net loss, and the trailing DPS is Rp18.6; we assume the dividend is suspended on our negative near-term earnings [S8, S0]. ESG is central rather than incidental: the strategy is a decarbonisation transition, the PLTU divestments cut emissions by about 80.0%, and the waste platform is the environmental-services asset, while governance is the weak link that has to earn its discount rather than assume it away [S9, S10, S16].

Indonesian holding companies owned through family or trust structures have long traded at persistent discounts to the value of the assets they control, because minorities depend on cash actually upstreamed and control rarely changes hands. A transition story can narrow the discount for a while, but the discount is the base rate, not the opportunity.

The nearest dated catalysts are the shareholder meeting to approve the HPS preference investment and the floating-solar commercial operation date [S15, S12]. The HPS transaction is the more important: the preference terms, the staging schedule and the first acquisition will tell us whether the waste platform's capital is raised on terms that leave value for the ordinary shareholder [S10, S15]. The KPIs we monitor are waste revenue and adjusted EBITDA share, Cora's collected tonnage and plant availability, coal cash cost and stripping ratio, the reserve statement, net debt to adjusted EBITDA, the holdco discount to our SOTP, and the HPS deployment schedule [S12, S9, S10]. We also watch related-party disclosures and any change in the preference terms, the channels through which waste value reaches the parent's ordinary shareholders [S8, S16]. Until a dated event or a waste re-rate changes the arithmetic, the balance of evidence supports **REDUCE** at the current price [S10, S15].

bear.narrative: The holdco discount widens ten points to 50%, above the card's band: coal prices fall, the HPS money is deployed slowly and the preference coupon absorbs waste cash, so the market pays less for the parts. This table shocks the discount only - the SOTP marks are dated holdings values and the consolidated forecast does not re-price them - and the report states that limitation plainly; the operating downside is shown separately as a driver-based corner (waste 7x floored at zero equity, coal zero, 50% discount), which is the SELL path.

bull.narrative: The holdco discount narrows ten points to 30%, the middle of the card's band, as waste EBITDA compounds on the HPS capital, coal cash cost stays low and the floating solar reaches COD on time. This table shocks the discount only, as the report states; the driver-based bull corner (waste 14.3x, coal +US$26m, 30% discount) is shown separately in section 4, not in this table.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Nine-month 2026 consolidated revenue was US$257.3m, 11% below the prior-year period, because the legacy coal business shrank faster than waste grew; the company's own release confirms this [S25, F179]. The nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter at the 2026 third-quarter run-rate of US$84.3m gives FY2026E of about US$341.6m, which is -6.6% against the FY2025 continuing-operations base of US$365.9m, not the -12% used before: the old figure implied a fourth quarter of US$64.7m, below every quarter of 2026 [S25, F1, F179]. We then return to 6%/5%/4%/3% as the HPS-funded waste build annualises and the 46 MWp floating solar starts producing [S25, S26, S12].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the latest actual: the company's 9M2026 release shows gross profit of US$45.2m on US$257.3m of revenue, which is 17.6% (the company rounds it to 18%), more than double the prior-year period's 8%, with waste plus electric vehicles at 66% of revenue [S25, F179, F180]. The waste segment's own gross margin is 13.3% while coal mining earned 35%; the blended ratio is therefore a mix outcome, not a waste margin [S25, F186, F188]. We anchor FY2026E at the exact 17.6% and hold it — there is no sourced reason for a margin fade, and a further uplift from waste mix is left to the bull case [S25].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The data pack's 11.4% is wrong: the LK shows selling and G&A expenses of US$71.95m against US$380.2m of segment revenue in FY2025 (18.9% of the reported US$365.9m consolidated revenue), and 1H 2026 sales and G&A were US$33.172m on US$173.016m (19.2%) [S17, S12, F96]. We hold the 1H 2026 run-rate of 19.2% rather than the previous 19.5%, which had no source [S12].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The full FY2025 D&A charge is US$74.121m (F81: fixed assets 22.205 + mine amortisation 31.317 + right-of-use 11.790 + intangibles 8.809), 20.3% of FY2025 revenue, and the engine history now carries that full charge, not the pack's 15.7 or the fixed-asset 22.2 alone [S8]. The 9M2026 release says the net loss includes Cora-related depreciation and amortisation that is largely non-cash, but it does not disclose the 9M charge [S25]. We therefore keep the post-divestment 1H 2026 run-rate: adjusted EBITDA 25.733 plus operating loss 4.770 implies a D&A plus PLN/other add-back of 30.503 on revenue 173.016 (17.6%, F98). The 20.3% FY2025 ratio includes divested-PLTU depreciation and higher mine amortisation and is not the forward run-rate [S12].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex was US$47.1m (12.9% of revenue), including mine-property additions of US$37.2m and fixed assets of US$9.8m [S8]. The 46 MWp floating-solar project is 65% complete with COD targeted for Q4 2026, so capex stays elevated: 10% in FY2026E, 9% in FY2027E and 8% long run [S12].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was US$9.1m on US$365.9m of revenue (2.5%), and the group describes disciplined working-capital management [S8, S3]. We hold 3.0% of revenue, above the actual to allow for the waste business's receivable build.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025's effective rate is meaningless on a loss; FY2024 paid US$14.1m on US$36.9m of pre-tax profit (38.2%), above the 22% statutory rate because of non-deductible items [S8]. We use the 22% statutory rate on positive pre-tax profit.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance costs were US$26.0m on opening debt of US$341.9m (7.6%); the June 2026 DBS-led syndicated facility of up to S$385m refinances the older loans [S8, S13]. We use 7.5% on opening debt.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income was US$3.9m on opening cash of US$67.8m (5.8%); 1H 2026 interest income was US$2.8m [S8, S12]. We use 5.5% on opening cash.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The June 2026 DBS-led facility of up to S$385m is for refinancing, working capital and subsidiary capex, so it is not purely refinancing [S13]. We model US$15m of net draws in FY2026E and US$10m in FY2027E for working capital and subsidiary capex, then zero: the HPS preference is capital at SBTH and does not sit at the parent [S10, S13]. The quarter-end debt line was flat ($392.9m at FY2025 vs $393.0m at 1H 2026), which caps the near-term draw [S8, S12].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries a one-off refinancing charge: the company states the 9M2026 net loss includes a one-off expense from the refinancing of the waste entities' senior loan, undertaken to lower the cost of capital, but discloses neither the amount nor the cash/non-cash split [S25]. We carry an explicit US$10-25m range and use US$18m, the mid-point, rather than a figure sized solely to reconcile the parent loss [S25, F182]. The charge is treated as cash and therefore inside the forecast net debt; if it is non-cash or amortised over the facility life, FY2026E net debt is lower by up to US$25m and the SOTP is unaffected because the SOTP marks do not use the forecast loss. Zero thereafter: the FY2025 PLTU divestment loss (US$96.9m) and the FX loss are non-recurring and excluded [S8, S17].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities were 40.7% of FY2024 net profit and the minority balance sheet interest is US$21.8m (about 11% of equity) at 1H 2026 [S8, S11]. At 9M2026 the total loss of US$40.05m against the US$35.4m parent loss implies the minorities absorbed about US$4.65m, 11.6% [S25, F126, F182]. We use 25%, allowing for the HPS preference claim at the waste subsidiary to sit ahead of the ordinary minority [S26].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 cash dividends were US$17.5m against a net loss, so the payout is not meaningful on negative earnings; the FY2024 DPS of Rp21.98 was paid out of a US$28.5m parent profit [S8, S0]. We assume 30% of parent profit once earnings recover, consistent with the historical record.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Shares rose from 8,249.4m at FY2025 to 8,309.6m at 1H 2026 as the MSOP/ESOP issued shares without pre-emptive rights; we assume 0.5% a year [S8, S11, S9].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Zeroed per QC round-2 Q2. The holdco_sotp target is SOTP plus a P/BV cross-check; no DCF method runs, so terminal growth drives nothing and the old 2.0% was an unconnected input. The field stays at zero so the engine's input contract is met without implying a growth assumption the valuation does not use [S0].

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: The base is the top of the card's 20-40% band, not the 45% the price happens to imply. The prior 45% was reverse-solved from the 30 October price, so the SOTP leg equalled the price by construction and carried no independent information [S0, S25]. The company does not publish a historical SOTP and the data pack has no NAV series, so a true five-year discount-to-NAV range cannot be sourced; the closest own-history series is P/BV (FY2022 0.929x, FY2023 0.489x, FY2024 0.566x, FY2025A 1.882x, mean 0.966x, median 0.748x) and the current trailing P/B is about 0.93x, at the own mean [S0]. VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT §2 sets 20-40% as the persistent base rate; 40% is the warranted top because the governance discount has not been earned away: Highland Strategic Holdings holds 60.356% through a Singapore trust and PT Toba Sejahtra another 7.975% [S9], the US$43.2m receivable sits with an undisclosed related party [S8], and the HPS preference ranks ahead of the ordinary at the waste subsidiary [S26, F195]. The dividend-upstream coverage proxy is only 1.22x nine-month operating cash flow against the annualised rule-of-thumb distribution, so the parent depends on subsidiary cash it does not control directly [F163]. There is no dated, completed narrowing catalyst: HPS is newly issued preference equity at SBTH, a financing rather than a cash distribution, and still needs EGMS approval [S26, F195, F197]. Section 4 shows the 30% band midpoint and the 40% top, and the 50%/30% scenario range around this base.

challenges.challenge: The waste mark, 55% of the gross parts, annualises the 9M average rather than the Q3 run-rate and is internally inconsistent with the report's own disclosures. 1H waste+EV EBITDA is 91.8% x US$25.733m = US$23.62m (F39, F24); 9M is 71% x US$44.4m = US$31.52m (S25, F181); the difference implies Q3 waste+EV EBITDA of only US$7.90m, or US$31.6m annualised - 25% below the US$42.03m used for the US$453.5m EV and US$218.7m equity mark. The revenue forecast itself uses the Q3 run-rate (US$84.3m) for Q4, so the waste mark is not using the same run-rate. At US$31.6m of EBITDA the waste equity is about US$106.2m (10.79x less the US$234.8m debt proxy), the SOTP is about Rp262, the blend about Rp262 and the target about Rp316, a -20% return (REDUCE), not HOLD. The prior response (F3) noted the Q3 mix shift but did not re-mark on it; the 9M LK segment note is the missing evidence.
challenges.answer: Rebuilt the waste mark from the period actuals. 1H waste+EV EBITDA is 91.8% x US$25.733m = US$23.623m (F39, F24); 9M is 71% x US$44.4m = US$31.524m (F141, F181); Q3 is therefore US$7.901m, or US$31.604m annualised (F145). At 10.79x less the US$234.793m debt proxy the waste mark is US$106.219m (F86), not US$218.7m. The 9M-average annualisation of US$42.032m and mark of US$218.732m are disclosed as F203/F204. The Q3 base gives SOTP Rp258 and a blended target of Rp312 (REDUCE); the 9M average gives Rp430 (F206), so the HOLD did depend on the 9M average. The base uses Q3 because the revenue build uses the Q3 revenue run-rate for Q4. Changed facts F145/F86/F146/F203/F204, the waste holding note and section I/4 of the report.

challenges.challenge: The base treats HPS as a zero-value preference inside SBTH, keeps the waste stake at 100% and carries no dilution, conversion or coupon sensitivity, although the terms are undisclosed. The report's own conversion math (F107-F110) shows S$555m could represent about 10% of SBTH at a US$3,673m pre-money value, 20% at US$1,632m, 30% at US$952m or 50% at US$408m; at the waste equity mark of US$218.7m, even a 10% common-equivalent stake would cost about US$22m, and a 30% stake about US$66m. The assumed 8-12% coupon is US$32.6-49.0m a year, 55-83% of the 9M annualised adjusted EBITDA of US$59.2m (not the 62-93% stated), and the report itself says the ordinary equity earns nothing until waste EBITDA covers the coupon, segment interest and sustaining capex - roughly double the 1H26 run-rate. A bear case that ignores the preference claim is not the most likely path.
challenges.answer: Added an explicit HPS conversion sensitivity: a 10%/20%/30% common-equivalent stake takes the blended target to Rp300.9/Rp289.8/Rp278.6 (F211-F213), all REDUCE, and the coupon-drag sensitivity is shown against the disclosed denominator. Corrected the coupon ratio to 55-83% of the US$59.2m annualised adjusted EBITDA (F101/F102 over F181), fixing C11 as well. The base still treats the preference as zero-value at inception because the cash raised and the prior claim are equal; the bear case now states that the ordinary earns nothing until the coupon is covered.

challenges.challenge: The SOTP omits the holdco-card deduction for holdco opex capitalised at about 10x. VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT section 1 requires "minus holdco opex capitalized at ~10x"; the report deducts only NCI and says parent-only third-party net debt is about nil, but no parent-level cost line is deducted. At an illustrative US$5-10m of parent-only opex, a 10x capitalisation is US$50-100m, or about Rp48-96 per share after the 45% discount and the two-thirds SOTP weight. The prior sign-off (QC Q3 NOTE) recorded this as uncapitalised "pending a sourced parent-only figure"; v8 still does not resolve it.
challenges.answer: The card point is already inside the segment marks. The Q2 segment note reconciles the full consolidated selling and G&A charge of US$33.172m (F96) to the five operating segments with no unallocated corporate column (S11 p.145), and the waste mark is struck on adjusted EBITDA after segment G&A while the coal run-off uses segment costs after selling and G&A (S12, S11 p.150). Capitalising the same group cost at 10x again would double count it. The residual is that any corporate cost embedded in the "others" book mark is not separately capitalised; that is disclosed in section 4. No parent-only PSAK 27 G&A figure exists in the registered filings, so a separate deduction cannot be sourced.

challenges.challenge: The "others" SOTP mark is US$43.6m of book net assets (F36-F37), but the US$43.2m non-current third-party receivable (F89) - the former Highland receivable assigned to CDG Trading at 6.8%, with CDG's ownership undisclosed - is roughly 99% of that net asset. The report classifies the receivable optics-class and half-haircuts it only in the P/BV leg (Rp263); the SOTP "others" mark carries it at full book, so the -Rp21.6m (half) or -Rp43.2m (full) haircut is applied to one leg and not the other. Goodwill of US$85.5m (F149) is about half of parent equity and is not haircut at all, and 9M CFO/EBITDA is 0.46x (F156) after 0.12x in FY2025 (F155).
challenges.answer: Applied the same optics-class half-haircut to the SOTP "others" mark: book net assets of US$43.649m less the US$21.581m half of the US$43.163m related-party receivable gives US$22.067m, so the SOTP and P/BV legs now carry the same treatment. Added a goodwill-impairment P/BV sensitivity (F210, about Rp108) and a cash-conversion bear in section 5 (9M CFO/EBITDA 0.46x, F156).

challenges.challenge: The update is a 30 September re-mark, but every balance-sheet input is 30 June: gross debt US$399.3m (F200), the segment debt proxies (F84/F85) and the NCI (F174) are 1H, and the 9M release discloses neither gross debt nor the financing cash flow. The 9M balance sheet has moved: assets US$751.68m vs US$764.42m, liabilities US$579.63m vs US$575.50m and equity US$172.04m vs US$188.92m (F135-F137, F28-F37), so leverage has worsened and the debt proxies may be stale. The report discloses the limitation but runs no sensitivity and does not say what net debt at 30 September could be.
challenges.answer: Disclosed a 30 September net debt proxy of US$313.8m from the disclosed cash of US$89.6m and the US$4.1m rise in total liabilities (F208), essentially the 30 June level, and ran a symmetric 5% debt-proxy sensitivity (F214/F215: target Rp293.4/Rp330.7). The base still uses the 30 June proxies because the 9M release discloses no gross debt; the limitation is stated in section 3.

challenges.challenge: Coal is marked at zero despite the strongest coal print of the year: 9M mining revenue US$61.8m, gross profit US$21.6m (35.0%) and EBITDA US$20.1m (S25, F187-F189), after a 1H operating loss of US$3.87m (F170). The report's own bull case adds only about US$26m of coal value, below the 9M annualised EBITDA of US$26.8m, and the base never shows the run-off DCF it says is "at or below zero." The US$120.4m debt proxy is an allocation of group interest, not a legal coal-secured claim, so the zero floor is a judgment, not a valuation, and the 9M actual has narrowed the evidence for it.
challenges.answer: Published the coal run-off on the disclosed actual volume, price, cash cost and 1H capex run-rate, with and without the US$120.4m debt proxy (F207). With the proxy the equity is negative, so the mark floors at zero; without the proxy the same US$120.4m would have to be deducted at holdco, leaving the SOTP unchanged. At the 3-4 Mt/yr plan the upper bound is about +US$26m before the proxy, which does not support a positive equity after it. The zero floor is therefore an allocation result, not a judgment.

challenges.challenge: The bull case shocks only the holdco discount (to 35%) and the waste multiple (14.3x); the operating drivers never rise. Waste revenue grew 41% in 9M (S25, F185), the HPS S$555m is intended for Asian waste expansion (S26, F196), the 46 MWp floating-solar project is 65% complete with COD targeted for Q4 2026 (S12, F53), and the EGMS to approve HPS is a dated event (S26, F197). None of these is a dated, valued bull case, and the report says there is "no dated narrowing catalyst" while listing the EGMS as the nearest dated catalyst in section 7.
challenges.answer: Added a dated bull case: the HPS EGMS and the deployment of the S$555m at a Cora-like multiple, the 46 MWp floating-solar COD in the fourth quarter, and waste revenue compounding at its nine-month rate, with the target at the peer-multiple case (F164) and the bull scenario value. Explained why the EGMS is not itself a discount-narrowing catalyst: it authorises preference equity that ranks ahead of the ordinary, so it changes the capital structure before the discount.

challenges.challenge: The 45% holdco discount is reverse-solved from the 30 October price, so the SOTP leg equals the price by construction (Rp397 vs Rp396) and the 7.1% expected return is a COE roll-forward of the price-anchored blend, not an independent value view. The card says the discount is the base rate, not the opportunity, and requires the current discount versus the name's own five-year range; the report only compares 45% with the card's 20-40% band and never shows the own-history range. The same circularity means the SOTP carries no information the price does not already carry, and the one-third P/BV cross-check at Rp263 drives the HOLD.
challenges.answer: The 45% discount was reverse-solved from the price, so the SOTP leg equalled the price. The base is now 40%, the top of the card band, justified by governance and upstream coverage (controlling trust, undisclosed related-party receivable, HPS preference ranking ahead, upstream coverage proxy F163), not by the price. A true five-year discount-to-NAV range cannot be sourced because the company publishes no historical SOTP and the data pack has no NAV series; the own-history P/BV range is disclosed instead. The 30% band midpoint gives a target of Rp346.5 (F205), still REDUCE.

challenges.challenge: The forecast is structurally loss-making through FY2035: gross margin 17.6%, opex 19.2% and D&A 17.6% give an EBIT margin of -1.6% in every year, so np_parent is negative from FY2026E to FY2035E and the 30% payout "once earnings recover" never pays a dividend. The report's thesis is that waste is the value driver, but the model never lets waste growth produce positive EBIT, and the P/BV leg applies 0.83x to a book that the model erodes by about US$25m a year. Either the margin structure is wrong or the P/BV cross-check is on a melting book.
challenges.answer: Added the P/BV stress on FY2027E and FY2028E forecast book (F209, about Rp225; lower on FY2028E book) and a full-goodwill-impairment case (F210, about Rp108), and removed the claim that the payout recurs. The report now says the forecast is EBIT-negative at the held margin structure and identifies the operating-leverage path: coal mine amortisation (F13) and coal segment G&A roll off as the 14 Mt reserve depletes. The base P/BV leg stays on current reported book; the primary SOTP does not depend on it.

challenges.challenge: The P/BV cross-check uses a 0.827x peer median, but the current CONGLOMERATES comps return ADRO 0.845502x, DSSA 2.838134x and IMJS 0.315071x - a median of 0.8455x, not 0.827x. The note itself records that the earlier 15.54x was a stale figure; this is the same class of error. The per-share effect is small (about Rp263 to Rp269), but the input should be refreshed and sourced.
challenges.answer: Stated the date and peer set the engine uses: the registered CONGLOMERATES packs at their 30 June 2026 balance sheets and current datapack prices give ADRO 0.8268x, DSSA 2.7501x and IMJS 0.2958x, median 0.8268x, so the P/BV leg is Rp263. The red team 0.8455x uses a later price snapshot not reproducible from the registered packs; the per-share effect is about Rp6 and does not change the rating.

challenges.challenge: The HPS coupon burden is stated as "62-93% of the 9M annualised adjusted EBITDA of US$59.2m (44.4 x 4/3)". The arithmetic gives 55.1% (32.647/59.2) to 82.7% (48.971/59.2), not 62-93%; the stated range uses a US$52.63m denominator, not the US$59.2m cited. The error overstates the bearish coupon burden by about 7-10 percentage points and is repeated in the assumptions note.
challenges.answer: Corrected the coupon burden to 55-83% of the US$59.2m annualised adjusted EBITDA (F101/F102 over F181); the old 62-93% used a US$52.63m denominator. The corrected ratio is repeated consistently in the assumptions note and the report.

challenges.challenge: The US$18m FY2026E refinancing one-off (other_nonop) is an unsourced estimate explicitly sized to make the full-year parent loss line up with the 9M actual. The release says the 9M loss includes a one-off refinancing expense but gives neither the amount nor the cash/non-cash split (S25); the number is therefore a plug, and the report does not show the target's sensitivity to it or whether it is a cash cost that affects net debt.
challenges.answer: Replaced the US$18m plug with an explicit US$10-25m range and use the US$18m mid-point; the release gives neither the amount nor the cash/non-cash split (S25). The note now states the charge is treated as cash and inside forecast net debt, that a non-cash or amortised treatment lowers net debt by up to US$25m, and that the SOTP is unaffected because the marks do not use the forecast loss.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull case only narrows the discount to 35% and lifts the waste multiple to 14.3x; it never lets the operating drivers rise. The 9M release shows waste revenue +41% and coal-mining EBITDA of US$20.1m after a 1H operating loss, yet the base marks coal at zero and the bull coal value is only about US$26m, below the 9M annualised coal EBITDA of US$26.8m, and the HPS-funded Asian waste expansion and the 46 MWp solar COD in Q4 2026 have no dated case. C6, C7.

missing_bear_case.note: Absent or understated: the undisclosed HPS preference terms (the report's own conversion math shows S$555m could take up to about 50% of SBTH), the implied Q3 waste-EBITDA slowdown, the US$43.2m CDG receivable sitting at book inside the SOTP "others" mark, the US$85.5m goodwill (about half of parent equity), 5.4x net debt/EBITDA and 0.46x 9M CFO/EBITDA. C2, C4, C5.

assumption_realism.note: The dominant mark annualises 9M waste+EV EBITDA (71% x US$44.4m x 4/3 = US$42.0m) while the report's own 1H share (91.8% x US$25.7m = US$23.6m) and 9M share (71% x US$44.4m = US$31.5m) imply only US$7.9m in Q3, or US$31.6m annualised; the revenue forecast itself uses the Q3 run-rate. The model is also structurally loss-making to FY2035 (opex 19.2% plus D&A 17.6% exceed the 17.6% gross margin), so the 30% payout "once earnings recover" never occurs. C1, C9.

evidence_and_citations.note: The 9M release facts verify verbatim (S25: 257.3, 45.2, 44.4, 35.4, 20.3, 89.6; coal EBITDA 20.1; waste 157.3 and 13.3%), and the D&A sum F81 is correctly labelled COMPUTED. But the full 9M LK is absent (the analyst discloses this), the P/BV peer median 0.827x no longer matches the comps (0.8455x), the coupon burden is mis-computed as 62-93% instead of 55-83%, and the US$18m refinancing one-off is an unsourced plug. C5, C10, C11, C12.

valuation_method_fit.note: Credit: the prior FATAL is fixed - the SOTP deducts only NCI, and the US$307.1m elimination is correctly excluded as the book consolidation wedge; the konglo/DSSA EV/EBITDA leg is dropped. But the waste multiple (10.79x) is the stock's own coal-era group median, not a waste-infrastructure mark; the 45% discount is reverse-solved from the current price, so the SOTP leg equals the price by construction (Rp397 vs Rp396) and no own-5y discount range is shown; the card-mandated holdco opex capitalisation at about 10x is missing; and HPS is not in the bridge. C3, C8.

bias_and_tone.note: Credit: the report refuses to book the HPS headline, discloses the P/BV counterweight and reports the preference coupon. But the HOLD is price-anchored: with the discount reverse-solved, the SOTP leg contributes no independent value, and the target is a mechanical COE roll-forward of the price-anchored blend. "The nine-month print supports the operating story" omits the Q3 waste slowdown. Doubling the bear weight would barely move the target because the bear shocks only the discount, not the marks. C1, C8.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The report records the look-through factors but reads no commodity or macro deck variable; the target is translated at spot USD/IDR 18,138 versus the house FY2027E 18,350 (about +1.2%, roughly Rp5/share), and the P/BV peer median is stale. The peer set (ADRO, DSSA, IMJS) mixes a konglo and coal names with a waste-dominant group. Credit: the konglo EV/EBITDA leg is dropped and the thermal-coal deck's neutral stance is not contradicted by a coal value. C10.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservative: coal zero, 45% discount (above the card's 20-40% band), minority 25% vs 11.6% implied actual, P/BV half-haircut of the receivable, 0.5% share growth. Optimistic: holdco opex omitted, no HPS dilution or coupon in the waste mark, 22% tax vs 38.2% last paid, stale P/BV median, and the 9M-average waste annualisation above the Q3 run-rate. The optimistic stack moves the rating (C1 alone takes the target to about Rp316, a REDUCE), so it is FATAL per the desk rule.

calibration.note: QC returns no BLOCK flags. The +4.2pp EBITDA-margin gap is below the 5pp gate and is explained by the 9M mix (17.6% gross margin vs 8.1% FY2025); FY2026E 16.0% is below the 9M actual 17.0%, so the forecast is conservative. Record hygiene only: the calibration.ebitda_margin justification is an orphan key and the 17.6% D&A is inferred, because the 9M LK does not disclose D&A.

signoff.notes: APPROVED on substance. FATAL C1 is fixed: waste is re-marked on the Q3 run-rate (US$31.6m annualised, F145; equity US$106.2m, F86), giving REDUCE Rp312, and the 9M-average alternative (F203/F204) with its Rp430.3 target (F206) is disclosed openly in the summary, thesis and section 4 - the base is the latest actual and matches the Q3 revenue build used for Q4, so the choice is honest and not hidden. C2-C9 answered on substance: HPS conversion sensitivity F211-F213; holdco-opex rebuttal sourced to S11 p.145 (full SG&A reconciled to five operating segments, no unallocated corporate column) with the residual limitation disclosed; receivable half-haircut now in both SOTP and P/BV legs plus goodwill and forecast-book stress; 30 Sep net-debt proxy F208 and symmetric debt-proxy sensitivity F214/F215; coal run-off DCF F207 with and without the debt proxy; dated bull case with EGMS and solar COD. C10-C12 MINOR addressed. QC FIX items cleared: Q1 - 9M collection now 755,990 t (S25/S22, F144) and the stale 1H 760k figure removed; Q2 - the ADD-band prose is corrected at line 113 (weighted Rp334.7 sits below price at the warranted discount). Lint PASS with 0 errors. No consensus contamination found. Director journal: lint advisories remain (4,760 words vs the 500-3,500 update range; only two valuation methods because the EV/EBITDA leg was deliberately dropped on L1 as konglo-inflated and segment-inconsistent); P/BV peer median 0.8268x vs the current comps 0.8455x (about Rp6/share, immaterial); Q6 residual - Q3 waste EBITDA is a residual of rounded share disclosures and the 9M segment note is still unfiled; 30 Sep gross debt undisclosed, so net debt is the F208 proxy.

bias.note: The Q3 run-rate is the most likely basis and is not mere caution: waste plus EV was 91.8% of 1H adjusted EBITDA but 71% of 9M, so the company's own disclosures imply Q3 waste-plus-EV EBITDA of 71% x US$44.4m less 91.8% x US$25.733m = US$7.901m, or US$31.604m annualised [S25, S12, F141, F181, F39, F24]. That is the last actual, the revenue build uses the same Q3 quarter for Q4 (US$257.3m less US$173.0m = US$84.3m), and the 9M average would give the older H1 two-thirds of the weight. The report discloses the alternative openly (9M mark US$218.7m, target about Rp430, F204/F206), so the choice is not hidden. The conservative elements (coal zero, 40% top-of-band discount, receivable half-haircut) are each sourced and argued, and they are offset by optimistic ones (22% tax vs 38.2% last paid, 16% FY2026E EBITDA margin below the 9M 17.3%, discount cut from 45% to 40%); net direction neutral. The Q3 residual is fragile (rounded shares from two documents, 9M segment note unfiled) - see Q6.

findings.finding: Section 1 states waste collection of about 760,000 tonnes in 1H 2026 [S15, F50], but the company's own 9M release reports 755,990 tonnes for 9M 2026 [S25, F144/S22]; a 9M total below the H1 figure is impossible, so one period is misstated.
findings.answer: Section 1 now reports the exact nine-month collection of 755,990 tonnes [S25, S22, F144] in place of the approximate 760,000-tonne first-half figure carried in the 22 October HPS announcement, which the later LK release supersedes and which had overstated the first half above the nine-month total. The F50 source quote and value are kept verbatim; its label records the supersession and that the 9M figure is used for the current period.

findings.finding: Section 5 says the probability-weighted driver target (F159, Rp334.7) 'is in the ADD band only because coal cannot go below zero'. Rp334.7 is 15.5% below the Rp396 price, not in an ADD band.
findings.answer: Rewrote the sentence: the driver-weighted target sits above the scenario-weighted base but below the current share price at the warranted discount, so it is not in an ADD band. The coal zero floor is now described as limiting how far the bear corner can fall, not as placing the weighted figure in ADD.

findings.finding: FY2035E roe 0.40 with np_parent -23.98m is an engine artefact (positive ROE on negative earnings); no target impact.
The calibration record labels model EBITDA margin 0.16 against FY2025A actual 0.12, while the FY2025A lines give 0.118; the 0.16 is the FY2026E forecast, so the record mixes periods.

The 10.79x waste multiple is the stock's own coal-era group EV/EBITDA median (FY2022 6.34x, FY2023 40.97x, FY2024 10.79x), not a waste-infrastructure mark; it is the swing input beside the run-rate choice. It is disclosed and defended because no premium-free waste comparator is registered.

Q3 waste EBITDA is a residual of two rounded share disclosures from different documents (S12 91.8% of 1H, S25 71% of 9M); the 9M LK segment note remains unfiled. The base is the latest actual and the report shows the US$42.0m 9M alternative, so no change is required, but the residual could be a trough if Q3 carried non-recurring waste cost.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'sotp': 0.6, 'pe': 0.25, 'pbv': 0.15}
flags.justification: The blend is now SOTP and P/BV only. The SOTP is a marked sum (coal at zero, waste on an EV/EBITDA multiple, the rest at book); P/BV uses the 0.8268x peer median on a different metric. The EV/EBITDA leg is dropped per the Sector Lead's L1: its 14.30x was DSSA's konglo-inflated multiple and it capitalised group EBITDA including the coal segment the SOTP marks at zero, so it cannot be rebuilt premium-free on a segment-consistent EBITDA inside the engine. Two methods (primary plus one cross-check) is the honest set here; P/E and dividend-yield legs are unavailable because trailing parent earnings are negative and no dividend is forecast [S0, S11, S12].
